text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Lawyers representing Malawi's main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) on Wednesday continued to oppose the presence of two foreign lawyers in an appeal case for a High Court ruling against government earlier this year.

The High Court in July nullified a bill passed by Parliament to mandate government to take over former president Kamuzu Banda's Press Trust. The trust runs the country's biggest conglomerate, the Press Corporation.

- Nine political parties, which are not represented in parliament and which are seeking to form a common front, will meet this weekend to discuss rampant corruption in government and public funds mismanagement.
- Two foreign nationals, one Zambian and a Dutch were arrested on Tuesday at Malawi's Lilongwe International Airport after they were found in possession of a suitcase containing 22 slabs of cannabis.
